card.name: Dollu Kunitha
card.era: Traditional; rooted in the Halumatha (Kuruba) Purana
card.tagline: Karnataka's vigorous Kuruba drum dance for Beereshwara
card.profile: Dollu Kunitha is a major drum dance of Karnataka performed chiefly by men of the Kuruba Gowda community, centred on the worship of the deity Beereshwara/Beeralingeshwara, a form of Shiva, around Chitradurga and Shivamogga (Wikipedia). Large double-headed drums (dollu), made from neem or palm with goat and sheep hide, are slung from the dancers' waists or necks and beaten with stick and hand while a group of 12-16 dancers move in circular and semi-circular formations led by a singer-conductor, often ending in a human chain (Amar Chitra Katha). Its origin myth, from the Halumatha/Kuruba Purana, tells of the demon Dolla-asura from whose skin Shiva fashioned the first drum.
card.insight: Embedded in temple worship - in Beereshwara temples the dollu hangs from the ceiling and is beaten at every act of worship - the dance is now performed across communities at festivals such as Maha Shivaratri and Ganesh Chaturthi (Village Square; Wikipedia).
